introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Elijah, exhausted and wanting to die, is fed by an angel and walks forty days to the mountain of God. In the Gospel, Jesus says, I am the living bread that came down from heaven; whoever eats this bread will live forever. Paul urges us to be kind and forgiving, imitating God. Let us receive the bread that gives us strength for the journey.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord feeds us with the bread of life. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may offer the bread of life to all who are weary on their journey. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are exhausted, depressed or without hope, like Elijah under the tree: that God may send someone to strengthen them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have drifted from the Eucharist: that the Father may draw them back to his Son. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families and communities torn by bitterness and anger: that they may learn to be kind and to forgive one another. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may taste and see that the Lord is good. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Faithful God, you fed Elijah in the desert and you feed us with the bread of life. Strengthen us for our journey and bring us to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Arise and eat
reflection.body:
Elijah has reached the end of his strength. Threatened with death, he flees into the desert, sits under a tree and prays to die: "It is enough. Now, O LORD, take away my life." Then he falls asleep. An angel wakes him gently: "Arise and eat!" There is bread and water beside him. He eats and sleeps again. The angel comes a second time: "Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you." And in the strength of that food, Elijah walks forty days to the mountain of God.

Many people today know Elijah's tiredness. God's answer to him was not a lecture, but food, rest and gentle care.

In the Gospel, the crowd grumbles about Jesus' claim to have come down from heaven: "Isn't this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" Jesus tells them that faith is a gift: "No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him." Then he speaks even more boldly: "I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh."

The Eucharist is food for the journey. We do not receive it because we are strong, but because "the journey is too great" for us without it.

Paul shows what this food produces in us: "be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you." The psalm invites us: "Oh taste and see that the LORD is good."

This week, if you feel like Elijah, tell God honestly, and let him feed you. Receive Communion as food for the road. And be the angel for someone else who is exhausted: bring them something, and stay with them a while.
